Framed Prints

The Frame Room

This is the room where our pictures arrive finished. Our print partner prints and frames each one when you order, at 12 by 18 inches, and it comes to you ready to hang. You are buying a finished piece here, not a file. If you would rather print and frame your own, the printable sets live on Paper & Pine.

Framed & ready to hang

These are The Road Back, Blue Ridge Layers at Dawn, Books and Candlelight, and the Outer Banks Lighthouse. All four started as printable sets, and the files are still on Paper & Pine. We offer them finished now for anyone who would rather skip the printing and framing. More designs will join them over time. We would rather add them properly than all at once.

How a framed print here is made, and hung

A short guide, because a finished picture is a bigger purchase than a file, and you should know exactly what happens between your order and your wall.

1

We draw it first

Every picture in this room started as our own artwork, drawn for one of our printable sets and looked over at full size before it was ever offered framed. Two of our pictures have been sent back and rebuilt before they earned a frame. The lighthouse story is in Studio Notes.

2

You order, then it is made

Nothing is pre printed. When you order, our print partner prints your picture and frames it for your order, one piece at a time. That is why colors can vary a touch from piece to piece, and why your piece is the only one exactly like it.

3

It arrives ready to hang

The framed print arrives finished at 12 by 18 inches. You do not need to buy a frame, cut a mat, or find a print shop. Take it out of the box and hang it.

4

Hang it where you live

Twelve by 18 is a kind size: big enough to hold a wall over a reading chair, a desk, or a hallway turn, and small enough to pair. Our day pictures and night pictures were made to sit together, so a morning piece and an evening piece from the same collection make an honest pair.

On size, plainly: every framed print in this room is 12 by 18 inches. Over a sofa, one piece reads as a quiet accent; two or three in a row carry the wall. Over a desk or beside a door, one is usually enough. If you are choosing between collections, the studio heroes are single strong scenes, a road, a ridge, a candlelit shelf, a lighthouse over quiet water, while the Magnolia and Pine pieces are quieter and reward a closer look.

On softness, plainly: a few of our older pictures were drawn at a smaller size and enlarged for framing, so their detail is soft and painterly up close by design, the way a painted canvas is soft up close. We say so here rather than pretend otherwise. At normal hanging distance they read exactly as they do in the pictures on this page.

On care: hang framed prints out of long direct sun, wipe the frame with a dry cloth, and let the picture be part of the room. These are made to be lived with, not kept in a closet.
